walkthrough: Goal: keep several artworks, find each again by its picture and title, start a new one, copy one before trying something risky, throw away one I no longer want, and find everything as I left it after the app was closed.

Entry: open OpenPaint on the tablet (2880 x 1800, landscape) on an empty library: a blank canvas. The top bar reads, left to right, Gallery (a button), then the grey undo and redo arrows; at its right end the Layers button. Draw a zigzag with the pen.

Tap Gallery: the artwork is stored and the gallery replaces the canvas. Its top bar reads Gallery at the left and has a plus at the right end. One card: the zigzag as a small white picture with an outline, under it the title Untitled Artwork, a copy button and a bin.

Tap the plus, then Screen size (since S14 the plus asks for a size): a new blank canvas opens at once, undo grey. Draw a triangle. Press the Android back button: the triangle is stored and the gallery shows two cards, the triangle first (the artwork changed last comes first), the zigzag second.

Tap the triangle's title: a Rename dialog drops in under the top bar (above where the keyboard rises), the rest of the screen dimmed, the field holding Untitled Artwork all selected and the keyboard up. Type Harbour sketch: it replaces the old title. Tap Done: the dialog closes and the card reads Harbour sketch. Cancel, the back button or a tap on the dimmed screen would have kept the old title; Done is grey while the field is empty.
Tap the copy button of Harbour sketch: a third card appears first, Harbour sketch with the same triangle; the original keeps its place.

Tap the zigzag's bin: a dialog in the middle of the dimmed screen asks Delete “Untitled Artwork”? This can't be undone, with Cancel and Delete. Tap Cancel: nothing changes. Tap the bin again and Delete: the zigzag's card is gone for good; two Harbour sketch cards remain.
Tap the first card's picture: the copy opens on the canvas, the triangle pixel for pixel, undo grey (history belongs to one visit). Tap Gallery to go back.

Leave the app and let the system close it, then open it again: it comes back to the gallery, where it was left, with both cards and their titles. Open the second card (the original) and draw a line across the triangle. Close the app from the canvas and open it again: the same artwork reopens on the canvas with the line. Press back: the gallery lists the changed original first.

Failure: a library call that fails shows a notice in the gallery's top bar with OK (could not read the gallery, open an artwork, make a new one, change the gallery); an artwork that cannot be opened stays in the library as it was. If storing fails when leaving the canvas, the canvas stays with Couldn't save and Retry. Not here: sorting by hand, selecting several, folders, import and export, a canvas size menu.
